category_title: Highly anxious students with ASD characterized by pervasive sensory rituals and wariness
minimal_context: The student and tutor are in the school dinner hall for a 20-minute session with a dog.
dialogue:
TUTOR: We are going to spend the next 20 minutes in the dinner hall with the dog.

STUDENT: (The student walks away, becoming very preoccupied with touching surfaces in the room and following markings on the floor in a repetitive manner.)

TUTOR: Please come back over here and look at the dog.

STUDENT: (The student continues performing mannerisms, showing an over-riding interest in the camera equipment rather than the dog.)

TUTOR: I am going to bring the dog closer to you now so you can see him.

STUDENT: (The student shows immediate wariness, watching the dog in order to move away as it gets too close, resulting in an anxious withdrawal.)

options.A: Understand the relationship between the student's 'fight' responses and anxiety, framing them into positive coping strategies.
options.B: Use contract rhetoric to regulate relations, requiring the student to declare daily targets and fill in weekly plans.
options.C: Use diverse pedagogical resources, such as documentaries and videos showing situations of animal cruelty or suffering.
options.D: Allow the student to choose how to structure and use the 20-minute sessions with the dog.
